1.explanation: The exported default function in src/languages/cmake.js defines the language grammar for CMake, including its `contains` array of highlighting modes. Currently it only registers `hljs.HASH_COMMENT_MODE` (single-line `#` comments) and lacks any mode to recognize the CMake multi-line comment delimiters `#[[` and `]]`. To fix the bug, this function must be updated to add a mode with `begin: /#\[\[/` and `end: /\]\]/` (className: 'comment') so that everything between `#[[` and `]]` is treated as a multi-line comment.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a CMake code block being highlighted by highlight.js where the user has written a multi-line comment using the CMake-specific syntax `#[[ … ]]`. Only the first line (`#[[test`) is grayed out (treated as a single-line comment), while the subsequent lines and closing `]]` are not highlighted as comments. Highlight.js is applying its generic `HASH_COMMENT_MODE` instead of recognizing the CMake multi-line comment delimiters.

2.explanation: The default export function in src/languages/cmake.js returns the syntax definition for CMake, including its comment rules under the contains array. Currently it only registers hljs.HASH_COMMENT_MODE (single-line comments starting with #). To support CMake’s multi-line comment syntax (#[[ ... ]]), this function’s contains array must be extended with a custom rule (e.g. begin:/#\[\[/, end:/\]\]/) so that the entire block is treated as a comment.
2.bug_scenario: When highlighting CMake code that uses multi-line comments of the form "#[[ ... ]]", only the first line (beginning with "#") is treated as a single-line comment and grayed out. The rest of the text inside the delimiters is not recognized as a comment and remains unstyled.
